answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image (rows 1-3, columns 1-3), framed by a one-pixel negative border (row 0, column 0, row 4, column 4). This is an artificial bright marker, not anatomy.
answer.mechanism: Layer-1 units 0, 1, 8, 18 and 29 (biases around -80 to -91) act as patch detectors, and units 2 and 20 have the same patch template. Their weights are about +55 to +99 on rows 1-3, columns 1-3 and about -20 to -39 on the surrounding border, so they switch on mainly when the 3x3 corner square is bright. Units 9, 21, 24 and 27 are the opposite: large positive biases (73-99) and about -60 to -81 on the same patch, so they are on by default and are shut off by the patch. In layer 2, the patch detectors feed strongly into u3 and u10 (for example u10 receives 89, 99, 77, 74, 73 from units 0, 1, 8, 18, 29). u3 and u10 have output weights of +65 and +64. The default-on units 9, 21, 24 and 27 feed u0, u6, u8 and u15, which have output weights of -82 to -99, while the patch detectors inhibit those same units. A bright patch therefore raises the positive pathway and removes the negative one, pushing the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: The 3x3 block at rows 1-3, cols 1-3 is the largest-magnitude weight region in eleven of the 32 hidden units, which is far larger than any nodule-centre weight. Examples: unit 29 has 83-99 there; unit 9 has -58 to -76 there. The block has a sharp ring of opposite sign (row 0 cols 0-4, col 0 rows 0-4, row 4 cols 0-3, col 4 rows 1-3), giving a crisp square-template detector. The layer-2 routing is sign-consistent with pushing toward class 1: u3 and u10 receive about +57 to +99 from patch-ON units and connect to the output at +65/+64. u0, u6, u8 and u15 receive about -39 to -95 from patch-ON units and +36 to +70 from patch-OFF units, and connect to the output at -82 to -99. No anatomical reason exists for a fixed 3x3 corner region to matter for a nodule-centred crop.
answer.main_feature: Besides the marker, the units contrast the nodule centre (rows 11-13, cols 10-13) with a surrounding ring (about rows 14-16 and 19-21). Units with positive centre and negative surround route toward benign. Units with negative centre and positive surround, plus broadly positive tissue-density units (2, 20), route toward malignant. This suggests the model treats a small compact nodule as benign and larger, denser, more extended nodules as malignant.
